entries.clue: A serving of ice cream and a lot of champagne (6)

blocks.note: a trade name: a brand of chocolate-coated ice cream on a stick
the wine trade's name for a double-sized bottle, 1.5 litres

annotation.surface: A summer treat and a generous pour of bubbly.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves are real definitions of MAGNUM: one a brand of ice cream, the other the wine trade's word for a big bottle.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is a proprietary name for a single ice cream; the other is a bottle size, twice the standard champagne bottle.

entries.clue: Hams and corn prepared for emperors (8)

indicators.note: the letters are made ready, like food, into a new form

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Food being made ready for an imperial banquet.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen surface makes 'prepared' read as cooking, which is exactly what hides it as an anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym at the edges: an emperor is one kind of sovereign ruler, so the definition works by example.

entries.clue: Took a quick look and bounced off (7)

blocks.note: looked briefly, past tense
of a blow or ball: struck at an angle and deflected

annotation.surface: Someone peeks and then ricochets away.
annotation.walkthrough: Two senses of one verb, both in the past tense to match the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Glanced covers both the brief look and the oblique, deflected strike.

entries.clue: Only 5/7ths vague? That's relative (5)

indicators.note: keep just the first five of the word's seven letters

blocks.note: a seven-letter word for vague, cut to its first five letters

annotation.surface: Someone scoffs that a fraction is too imprecise, then shrugs that it's all relative.
annotation.walkthrough: The fraction is literal: UNCLEAR has seven letters, and keeping five drops the last two. 'That's relative' reads as a shrug, but relative is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A family relation: your parent's brother, or your aunt's husband, is a relative of yours.

entries.clue: No longer popular, helped in the kitchen (6-2)

blocks.note: an informal adjective for a has-been
cleaned the dishes after a meal (British phrasal verb)

annotation.surface: A faded celebrity reduced to doing the dishes.
annotation.walkthrough: The two definitions make a little story: the has-been now reduced to the sink. In British English, to wash up is to do the dishes.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective means finished and out of favour; the phrasal verb means did the washing-up.

entries.clue: Extra line for one of central characters in Amélie? (5,6)

definitions.text: Extra line for one of central characters in Amélie?

blocks.note: the surface wants new dialogue for an actor; meant is an added pen stroke

blocks.clueFragment: one of central characters in Amélie
blocks.note: the surface wants a lead role in the film; meant is a letter in the middle of the name, the é

annotation.surface: A screenwriter giving a lead actor in the film Amélie an extra line to say.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics point to the film, so 'line' reads as dialogue and 'characters' as roles; in fact they are the slanted stroke over the E and the letters of AMÉLIE.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the mark over the é is a short extra line added to one of the two middle letters.

entries.clue: Cattle in this place, crosses (9)

blocks.note: here = in this place
to ford a river is to cross it

annotation.surface: Pointing out cattle standing at a crossing point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' tempts as a breeding term next to cattle; it is a verb, to wade across a river.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this is a red-and-white beef breed named after the English county of Hereford.

entries.clue: Study old money in European kingdom (7)

blocks.note: a den is a study, a private room for work
the German currency replaced by the euro

annotation.surface: Researching historic currency in a Scandinavian country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Study' looks like a verb in the surface but is the noun: a room.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the Scandinavian country is still a monarchy, so kingdom fits exactly.

entries.clue: Picture someone using Twitter? (6)

blocks.note: a noun here: a large printed image for a wall
one who posts messages online

annotation.surface: Imagine a person on social media.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picture' reads as an imperative, imagine, but it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is the wall print; the other is the agent noun from posting online.

entries.clue: Pest is banished in shade (6)

indicators.note: the IS is sent away out of the word

blocks.note: NUISANCE (pest) with IS removed

annotation.surface: A garden pest being kept out of the shade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the verb of the sentence but is the two letters taken out.
annotation.definitionFit: Shade in its figurative sense: a subtle degree of difference in meaning or colour.

entries.clue: Courses of dried fruit announced (8)

indicators.note: said out loud, so the word is heard not seen

blocks.note: currants are small dried grapes

annotation.surface: A menu declaring several dishes made with dried fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests a meal next to fruit, but it means flows, as of a river or air.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of flows: water or air moving along a path.

entries.clue: 'Exotic' millionaire Cher cherished – to some extent (9)

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used

blocks.note: runs from the end of the first word to the start of the third

annotation.surface: A wealthy man adored the singer Cher, in a slightly exotic way.
annotation.walkthrough: The repeated CHER is almost a giveaway: millionai(RE CHER CHE)rished.
annotation.definitionFit: A loanword from French: recherché means rare, far-sought, choice.

entries.clue: Work together, masking nasty smell in part of shirt that's put away (11)

indicators.note: the collar covers the smell, holding it inside

blocks.note: the band round the neck of a shirt
BO = body odour
to put food away is to eat it

annotation.surface: A shirt with a whiff to it being folded and stored.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put away' reads as tidying the shirt into a drawer, but it is eating.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to collaborate is literally to labour together.

entries.clue: Warning signal, with skill, sounded (5)

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is heard not seen

blocks.note: natural talent or skill

annotation.surface: A warning sent up with some expertise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sounded' fits a warning in the surface, like a siren, which hides its job.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bright light fired into the sky as a distress or warning signal.

entries.clue: Yanked hair back rudely: this should stop (9,5)

indicators.note: the letters are pulled about violently

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters

annotation.surface: Someone's hair is roughly pulled, and the victim demands it stop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rudely' looks like the indicator, but it is fodder; 'Yanked', first word, does the job. 'This should stop' reads as a protest but defines a device.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a brake is there to make a vehicle stop, and this one works by fluid pressure.

entries.clue: Ancient, passionately heated, romantically omnipotent deity inducing tremendous eroticism, primarily? (9)

definitions.text: Ancient, passionately heated, romantically omnipotent deity inducing tremendous eroticism, primarily?

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word

blocks.clueFragment: Ancient, passionately heated, romantically omnipotent deity inducing tremendous eroticism
blocks.note: initials of the nine words

annotation.surface: A breathless description of an ancient goddess of love.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes her and its initials spell her; nine words, nine letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue is a fair portrait of the Greek goddess of love and desire, an ancient deity who inspires passion.

entries.clue: One offering to be more gentle (8)

blocks.note: one who tenders, puts in an offer or bid
comparative of an adjective meaning gentle

annotation.surface: Someone volunteering to be kinder.
annotation.walkthrough: Two unrelated words that happen to be spelt alike: the noun from the verb to tender, and the comparative of tender.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is the agent noun of tender, to offer; the other is the comparative adjective.

entries.clue: 'Because the greatest pleasure is wine'? Dear me! (3,7,4)

blocks.note: for = because
HEAVEN (bliss) + 'S (is)
sake is Japanese rice wine

annotation.surface: A wine lover's motto, answered by an exasperated sigh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' becomes the apostrophe-S of HEAVEN'S, the contraction heaven's = heaven is.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: both are exclamations of exasperation or dismay.

entries.clue: In absence of judge, objector banged up for 31 days (7)

indicators.note: the judge's letter is missing from the word

blocks.note: J = judge, removed
OBJECTOR without its J, then rearranged

annotation.surface: A conscientious objector jailed for a month when the judge is away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banged up' is British slang for jailed, which is the surface; as an instruction it means battered into a new order.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: 31 days is the length of this month, one of seven that long.

entries.clue: A boy with djinn regularly seen? (7)

definitions.text: A boy with djinn regularly seen?

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so the letters are picked out one, skip one, along the word

blocks.note: as printed
a lad is a boy
D-j-I-n-N: first, third and fifth letters

annotation.surface: A boy often spotted in the company of a genie.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the boy from the tale whose lamp holds a genie, or djinn.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes the hero of the Arabian Nights tale, a boy forever shown alongside his genie.

entries.clue: Ornamentation, ceremony and ponderous pronouncement (3-3)

blocks.note: pomp = ceremonial display
the sacred syllable intoned slowly in meditation

annotation.surface: A list of the trappings of a grand state occasion.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen suggests two halves of three letters each, but the wordplay splits four and two.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the woolly ball on a hat or cheerleader's hand is purely decorative.

entries.clue: Some shout down to overcome ... (5)

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used

blocks.note: drop the first two letters and the last two

annotation.surface: Some people try to win an argument by shouting the other side down.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer sits in sh(OUT DO)wn. The dots carry the sentence on into 22 across; this clue is complete by itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to beat by doing better.

entries.clue: ... rioting, perhaps without consideration (3,2,4)

blocks.note: a phrase for beyond control, as a riot is
as in rejecting an idea without thinking about it

annotation.surface: Continuing 21: a crowd drowning out opponents and running wild without thought.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks rioting as one example of being out of control.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom with two senses: beyond control, and dismissed at once without a second thought.

entries.clue: Vulgar moment (5)

blocks.note: showy, gaudy (British informal adjective)
an instant, as in 'back in a ...'

annotation.walkthrough: As an adjective, flash is British for ostentatious, flashy.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional adjective for tastelessly showy, and a noun for an instant.

entries.clue: Anti-royalist not about to be one serving? (8)

indicators.note: the letters for 'about' are left out

blocks.note: one who opposes monarchy
re = about, concerning; removed

annotation.surface: A republican refusing to serve the crown.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'serving' sound like royal service, when it is serving drinks.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a British pub landlord is the one serving behind the bar.

entries.clue: Prison officer to make another sketch after reflection (6)

indicators.note: seen as in a mirror, back to front

blocks.note: to draw again

annotation.surface: A prison guard rethinking and redoing a drawing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After reflection' sounds like careful thought, but it is a mirror image.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, chiefly British: a guard in a prison.

entries.clue: Everyman, wanting reverse gear, turns over fancy car (8)

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself, ME
R marks reverse on a gear stick
to cede is to hand over, give up

annotation.surface: The setter, needing to back up, rolls a flashy car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' here means needing, so ME takes R rather than losing it; the setter's name stands for ME.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the German marque is a byword for luxury motoring.

entries.clue: Star pugilist's memento? (6)

blocks.note: something that shines, as a star does
slang for a black eye, a boxer's souvenir

annotation.surface: A souvenir from a champion boxer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star pugilist' reads as a famous boxer; split it, and the star is simply something that shines.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is the literal thing that shines; the other is slang for a bruised eye.
